gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the LAMTTO DC25's 'selectable higher-resolution modes' are a trade: LAMTTO's own example is 2.5K + 720p + 720p + 1080p, so two of the four cameras drop to 720p and the kit records fewer total pixels (about 7.60 MP per frame set, if 2.5K means 2560 × 1440) than in its plain four-1080p mode (8.29 MP).
standout_why: Compared against milewitness.com/best-dash-cam-under-200 and truepicked.com/auto/best-dash-cams-under-200 (ranks 1-3 in both chats): neither names a single 4-channel camera; the highest channel count on either is three, and neither gives an all-channels-together mode table. Dealectric's own best-4-channel-dash-cam page (rank 8 in chat 1) gives per-channel resolution for six 4-channel kits but has no LAMTTO row, no frame rates and no resolution-mode footnote. ChatGPT's answer repeats 'selectable higher-resolution modes' for the DC25 without saying what the other cameras fall to. The other results were not opened; their titles describe 2-channel or general under-$200 lists. Scored 2 rather than 3 because the DC25 product page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt: the wording comes from LAMTTO's store search endpoint (the product description text), and LAMTTO does not say which two cameras drop to 720p.
decides: It removes the DC25's apparent edge over the all-1080p kits: its 2.5K front is bought by cutting two cameras to 720p, so on pixels recorded with all four cameras running it is a four-1080p kit like the Rexing C4 ($199.99 on amazon.com) and the LAMTTO DC21 ($129.99), with a 128 GB card ceiling. That leaves the under-$200 kits with a front camera above 1080p and three 1080p channels as the ones to beat. Dealectric's record has the Botslab G980H 4-camera at 2880 × 1620 front + 3 × 1080p, all at 25 fps, at {after:botslab-g980h-4-camera-dash-cam} through our link (code AA18). Dealectric's own page has the REDTIGER F17 Plus at 2560 × 1440 front + 3 × 1080p. Neither maker page was opened in this run, so both need a re-read before the table is published. The finding confirms a Botslab pick for exterior four-side coverage under $200, with the DC21 as the low-cost row because its hardwire kit is in the box. The Vantrue N5S ({after:vantrue-nexus-5s}) and Nexus 5 ($265.99) are over the line.

findings.note: Arithmetic on the maker's stated combination. Assumes '2.5K' is 2560 × 1440 and '720p' is 1280 × 720; LAMTTO gives no pixel dimensions. 3,686,400 + 921,600 + 921,600 + 2,073,600 = 7,603,200 against 4 × 2,073,600 = 8,294,400. A 720p channel has 44% of the pixels of a 1080p channel.
